question: There are four nodes connected by directed edges. Node 1, which could represent the starting point, is connected to two other nodes: There is an edge from node 1 to node 2 with a capacity of 8. There is an edge from node 1 to node 3 with a capacity of 7. Node 2 is situated at the top of the graph and acts as an intermediate node, with three edges connected to it: An edge leading from node 2 to node 3 with a capacity of 2. An edge leading from node 2 to node 4 with a capacity of 4. Node 3 is another intermediate node and has two edges: An edge from node 3 to node 4 with a substantial capacity of 12. Node 4, which could represent the target or terminal, does not have any edges leading to other nodes, implying that it could be the end point. Find the corresponding maximum flow of the graph. Provide your answer rounded to the nearest integar.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "nodes": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "arcs": [(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4)],
    "capacity": {
        (1, 2): 8,
        (1, 3): 7,
        (2, 3): 2,
        (2, 4): 4,
        (3, 4): 12,
    },
    "source": 1,
    "sink": 4,
    "intermediate_nodes": [2, 3],
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=d["nodes"])
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=d["arcs"], dimen=2)
    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["intermediate_nodes"])

    # flow variable on each arc; domain NonNegativeReals
    # assumption: flow_variable_domain (text silent)
    model.f = pyo.Var(
        model.A,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=lambda m, i, j: (0, d["capacity"][(i, j)]),
    )

    # capacity: flow <= capacity on each arc
    # "an edge from node 1 to node 2 with a capacity of 8"
    def cap_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.f[i, j] <= d["capacity"][(i, j)]

    model.cap = pyo.Constraint(model.A, rule=cap_rule)

    # intermediate node conservation: outflow - inflow == 0
    # "Node 2 ... acts as an intermediate node" / "Node 3 is another intermediate node"
    def cons_rule(m, k):
        out = sum(m.f[k, j] for (i, j) in d["arcs"] if i == k)
        inn = sum(m.f[i, k] for (i, j) in d["arcs"] if j == k)
        return out - inn == 0

    model.cons = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=cons_rule)

    # source net outflow >= 0
    # assumption: source_balance_direction
    def source_rule(m):
        out = sum(m.f[d["source"], j] for (i, j) in d["arcs"] if i == d["source"])
        inn = sum(m.f[i, d["source"]] for (i, j) in d["arcs"] if j == d["source"])
        return out - inn >= 0

    model.source_balance = pyo.Constraint(rule=source_rule)

    # sink net outflow == -flow value
    # assumption: sink_balance_direction
    def sink_rule(m):
        out = sum(m.f[d["sink"], j] for (i, j) in d["arcs"] if i == d["sink"])
        inn = sum(m.f[i, d["sink"]] for (i, j) in d["arcs"] if j == d["sink"])
        return out - inn == -m.flow_value

    model.flow_value = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.sink_balance = pyo.Constraint(rule=sink_rule)

    # objective: maximize sum of flows on arcs leaving the source
    # "Find the corresponding maximum flow of the graph"
    # assumption: objective_quantity
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.f[d["source"], j] for (i, j) in d["arcs"] if i == d["source"])

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model
